name: python-observability
description: Python observability for logging, metrics, tracing, correlation IDs, dashboards, and debugging.

Emit production logs as JSON with consistent, machine-readable fields; local development may use human-readable formats. Track latency, traffic, errors, and saturation at every service boundary. Thread a unique ID through all logs and spans for each request. Keep metric label values bounded. Unbounded labels (like user IDs) explode storage costs.

Configure `structlog` with `structlog.contextvars.merge_contextvars`, `structlog.processors.add_log_level`, `structlog.processors.TimeStamper(fmt="iso")`, `structlog.processors.StackInfoRenderer()`, `structlog.processors.format_exc_info`, and `structlog.processors.JSONRenderer()`. Use `logger = structlog.get_logger()` and fields `correlation_id`, `method`, `path`, `user_id`, `duration_ms`, `error_type`, `error_message`. Every log entry should include standard fields for filtering and correlation. Use levels consistently: `DEBUG` diagnostics; `INFO` lifecycle/operations; `WARNING` recoverable anomalies; `ERROR` failures needing attention. Never log expected behavior at `ERROR`. A user entering a wrong password is `INFO`, not `ERROR`.

Generate a unique ID at ingress and thread it through all operations:
`correlation_id: ContextVar[str] = ContextVar("correlation_id", default="")`
`cid = request.headers.get("X-Correlation-ID") or str(uuid.uuid4())`
`set_correlation_id(cid)`; `response.headers["X-Correlation-ID"] = cid`
Propagate outbound correlation IDs with `httpx.AsyncClient` and `headers={"X-Correlation-ID": correlation_id.get()}`.
